tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

details.reference: BP Monograph for Colloidal anhydrous silica

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat once if not dissolved; add 0.9 mL, then 2 mL, then 7 mL solvent with the same steps to classify; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL, then 1 mg in 10 mL, else practically insoluble. Solvent list not extracted (see STM text).

details.reference: BP (SC IV K.) Characters Section in Monographs

tests.procedure: Identification (reaction of silicate): in a platinum crucible put about 10 mg sodium fluoride R and a few drops of sulfuric acid R to give a thin slurry with about 20 mg of the sample; cover with a thin transparent plastic plate with a drop of water R suspended beneath; warm gently. A white ring must form rapidly around the drop of water.

details.reference: BP 2025 Monograph for colloidal anhydrous silica

tests.procedure: pH: shake 1.0 g sample with 30 mL carbon dioxide-free water; measure with a calibrated pH meter.

details.reference: BP 2025 Monograph for colloidal anhydrous silica

tests.procedure: Chlorides (limit test): 1.0 g + 20 mL dilute nitric acid and 30 mL water, water bath 15 min with frequent shaking; dilute to 50 mL if needed, filter, cool; dilute 10 mL of filtrate to 15 mL; add 1 mL dilute nitric acid, pour into a tube with 1 mL silver nitrate solution R2. Standard: 10 mL chloride standard solution (5 ppm Cl) + 5 mL water treated the same way. After 5 min protected from light, opalescence in the sample must not exceed the standard (NMT 250 ppm).

details.standardCl: 10 mL chloride standard solution (5 ppm Cl)

tests.procedure: Loss on ignition: weigh a dry crucible (W1); weigh 0.2 g sample into it (W2); ignite in muffle at 900 ± 50 °C for 2 h; cool in desiccator; weigh the crucible with the ignited substance (W4); W3 = W1 + W2; loss on ignition (weight) = W3 - W4. Limit NMT 5.0%.

details.formula: W3 = W1 + W2; loss = W3 - W4 (% formula not written in the STM)
details.reference: BP 2025 Monograph for colloidal anhydrous silica

tests.procedure: Assay (SiO2, gravimetric, with the loss-on-ignition residue): moisten the residue with 0.2 mL sulfuric acid R and enough ethanol (96%) R; add 6 mL hydrofluoric acid R and evaporate to dryness on a hot plate at 95-105 °C; wash the sides with 6 mL hydrofluoric acid R and evaporate to dryness; ignite at 900 ± 50 °C, cool in desiccator and weigh. The difference between the final residue and the loss-on-ignition residue gives the SiO2 content. Limit 99.0-100.5% (ignited substance).

details.reference: BP 2025 Monograph for colloidal anhydrous silica

openQuestions.question: Minimum quantity: the spec sheet gives 100 g routine; the STM gives 70 g routine and retention and 50 g periodic retest. Routine 100 g from the spec, retention 70 g and retest 50 g from the STM; confirm the routine quantity.
